title: Characterizing the Impact of GPU Power Management on an Exascale System
problem: Exascale GPU-accelerated HPC systems must balance energy consumption control with throughput preservation. Frequency and power capping provide runtime tuning but operate via distinct hardware paths and affect workloads differently.
motivation: As systems approach exascale, energy management becomes critical. Leadership-class systems like Frontier provide multiple energy control mechanisms, but their relative effectiveness across diverse workloads remains poorly characterized.
method: Comprehensive empirical evaluation on Frontier (AMD MI250X-based exascale system) using diverse HPC proxy applications. Tests frequency and power capping at multiple levels, node counts (1 and 32), measuring performance-energy trade-offs across varied application profiles.
key_novelty: Systematic characterization of frequency vs. power capping effectiveness on exascale GPU systems; practical guidelines for energy tuning; analysis of scalability impacts across single-node and multi-node scenarios.
contributions: Comprehensive evaluation of GPU frequency and power capping on leadership-class exascale system
Quantification of performance-energy trade-offs across capping levels and node counts
Demonstration that frequency capping achieves up to 13.2% energy efficiency gains without performance loss
Practical guidelines for system administrators balancing energy and performance

metrics.energy_efficiency_gain: Up to 13.2% without performance loss (frequency capping)
metrics.performance_loss: Minimal with frequency capping; more significant with power capping

limitations: Study focused on Frontier; generalization to other GPU architectures unknown; abstract lacks specifics on application categories
primary_theme: GPU Energy Management on Exascale Systems
